title: 358. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Area of a Circular Sector
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the area of a sector using the degree-measure formula.
questions.question: A sector of a circle has radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and central angle \(60^\circ\). What is the area of the sector?
questions.explanation:
Use the sector area formula \(A=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^2\). Substitute \(\theta=60^\circ\) and \(r=6\):
\[
A=\frac{60}{360}\pi(6)^2=\frac{1}{6}\pi\cdot 36=6\pi.
\]
So the area of the sector is \(6\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: A sector is a fraction \(\frac{\theta}{360}\) of the full circle area \(\pi r^2\).

questions.learningObjective: Apply the sector area formula to a right-angle sector.
questions.question: A sector of a circle has radius \(10\text{ cm}\) and central angle \(90^\circ\). What is its area?
questions.explanation:
Use \(A=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^2\). Since \(90^\circ\) is \(\frac{1}{4}\) of a full circle,
\[
A=\frac{90}{360}\pi(10)^2=\frac{1}{4}\pi\cdot 100=25\pi.
\]
Therefore, the sector area is \(25\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: A \(90^\circ\) sector is one quarter of the full circle.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate sector area when the central angle is given in radians.
questions.question: A sector has radius \(8\text{ m}\) and central angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) radians. What is its area?
questions.explanation:
When the central angle is in radians, use \(A=\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta\). Substitute \(r=8\) and \(\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}\):
\[
A=\frac{1}{2}(8)^2\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)
=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 64\cdot \frac{\pi}{3}
=\frac{32\pi}{3}.
\]
So the area is \(\frac{32\pi}{3}\text{ m}^2\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the central angle of a sector from its area and radius.
questions.question: A sector has area \(12\pi\text{ cm}^2\) and radius \(6\text{ cm}\). What is its central angle in degrees?
questions.explanation:
Use \(A=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^2\). Substitute the known values:
\[
12\pi=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi(6)^2
=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi\cdot 36
=\frac{\theta}{10}\pi.
\]
Divide both sides by \(\pi\):
\[
12=\frac{\theta}{10}.
\]
Thus \(\theta=120^\circ\).
questions.hint: Substitute the given area and radius into the sector area formula, then solve for \(\theta\).

questions.learningObjective: Find the radius of a sector from its area and central angle.
questions.question: A sector has area \(18\pi\text{ cm}^2\) and central angle \(80^\circ\). What is the radius of the sector?
questions.explanation:
Using \(A=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^2\),
\[
18\pi=\frac{80}{360}\pi r^2
=\frac{2}{9}\pi r^2.
\]
Divide both sides by \(\pi\):
\[
18=\frac{2}{9}r^2.
\]
So
\[
r^2=18\cdot\frac{9}{2}=81,
\]
and therefore \(r=9\text{ cm}\).

questions.learningObjective: Calculate sector area after converting diameter to radius.
questions.question: A circle has diameter \(14\text{ cm}\). A sector of this circle has central angle \(45^\circ\). What is the area of the sector?
questions.explanation:
The radius is half the diameter, so \(r=7\text{ cm}\). Use \(A=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^2\):
\[
A=\frac{45}{360}\pi(7)^2
=\frac{1}{8}\pi\cdot 49
=\frac{49\pi}{8}.
\]
Thus the sector area is \(\frac{49\pi}{8}\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: First convert the diameter to radius, then apply the sector area formula.

questions.learningObjective: Use proportionality to compare sector areas in the same circle.
questions.question: In a circle, a sector with central angle \(120^\circ\) has area \(24\pi\text{ cm}^2\). In the same circle, another sector has central angle \(60^\circ\). What is the area of the second sector?
questions.explanation:
For sectors in the same circle, the radius is the same, so sector area is proportional to the central angle. The angle ratio is
\[
\frac{60^\circ}{120^\circ}=\frac{1}{2}.
\]
Therefore the area of the second sector is
\[
\frac{1}{2}\cdot 24\pi=12\pi.
\]
So the area is \(12\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: For sectors of the same circle, compare their central angles to compare their areas.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate sector area for a non-special central angle.
questions.question: A sector has radius \(9\text{ cm}\) and central angle \(120^\circ\). What is the area of the sector?
questions.explanation:
Use \(A=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^2\). Since \(\frac{120}{360}=\frac{1}{3}\),
\[
A=\frac{1}{3}\pi(9)^2
=\frac{1}{3}\pi\cdot 81
=27\pi.
\]
Therefore, the sector area is \(27\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: A \(120^\circ\) sector is one third of the full circle.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the radius using sector area and arc length.
questions.question: A sector has area \(15\pi\text{ cm}^2\) and arc length \(5\pi\text{ cm}\). What is the radius of the sector?
questions.explanation:
Use the relation \(A=\frac{1}{2}rL\), where \(L\) is the arc length. Substitute \(A=15\pi\) and \(L=5\pi\):
\[
15\pi=\frac{1}{2}r(5\pi).
\]
So
\[
15\pi=\frac{5\pi}{2}r.
\]
Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{2}{5\pi}\) gives
\[
r=6.
\]
Thus the radius is \(6\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Sector area can be written as \(A=\frac{1}{2}rL\), where \(L\) is the arc length.

questions.learningObjective: Determine arc length from sector area and radius.
questions.question: A sector has radius \(12\text{ cm}\) and area \(24\pi\text{ cm}^2\). What is its arc length?
questions.explanation:
Use \(A=\frac{1}{2}rL\). Substitute \(A=24\pi\) and \(r=12\):
\[
24\pi=\frac{1}{2}(12)L=6L.
\]
Divide both sides by \(6\):
\[
L=4\pi.
\]
Therefore, the arc length is \(4\pi\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use \(A=\frac{1}{2}rL\) and solve for the arc length \(L\).
